title: Dick James resigns from Northern Songs | 1970
content:
Dick James, the music publisher who founded Northern Songs with Beatles manager Brian Epstein, resigned from the company on 14 August 1970.

The Beatles lost control of Northern Songs on 19 September 1969, when ATV took a 54% controlling stake in the company.

ATV had handed the management of Maclen Music, which handled Lennon and McCartney’s Beatles-era compositions for North America and the Philippines, to Don Kirshner’s Kirsher Entertainment Corporation. Maclen had previously been controlled by Northern Songs.

ATV also announced on this day that they would continue the management of Northern Songs in the UK and other territories, but that the contract between Maclen and Dick James, Inc had been terminated. As a result, James resigned on this day as managing director and board member of Northern Songs.
